KNOWN_PREFILLS.nameBoxExamined: OCP-4/Print is the one held fact this packet does not print, and it was read against the contract rather than accepted on the builder's word. Measured first hand from the pinned binary: 'Print' is ONE text widget, x 37.8 w 350.4 h 9.84, and the source page prints three sub-captions beneath it - 'Last Name' at x 90, 'First Name' at x 203, 'Middle Name' at x 330 - so a single left-edge value lands under Last Name whatever it contains. The shared finalizer's only multi-fact channel joins facts with a newline (rcap-official-form-finalize.mjs, composedText = values.join('\n')) into a 9.84 pt box, so the mechanism to place three parts at three x positions does not exist. Against the completeness contract's GENUINELY UNAVAILABLE condition, availability is 'written elsewhere in this packet or carried in the field map's factMap' (verify-packet-completeness.mjs lines 331-341, 380): the name is written nowhere in this one-page packet and appears in no factMap, so the REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING declaration holds on the contract's own terms. The blank is disclosed twice in participant-instructions.md, with the measurement and with an instruction to print the name in the three captions' order. This is recorded, not scored as a missing known prefill.

REPEATING_ROWS.measured: MEASURED, not deferred. OCP-4 carries no repeating group, and the enumeration is the measurement. All 23 AcroForm widgets were read first hand from the pinned binary with their rectangles, and all 23 flattened appearances were read back from each delivered fixture, so the enumeration covers the whole form: 13 single text blanks, 3 signature widgets, and 7 check boxes. Test 1 - field names carrying a row index (Name:1, Name:2, Name_1): 0 of 23. Test 2 - y-bands sharing an identical multi-column signature, which is what a repeating row group is: 0. The four identity bands each occur exactly ONCE and carry different printed captions - y 552.72 (Print, Date of Birth), y 501.96 (Mailing address, City, State, Zip), y 481.92 (Occupation, Social Security, Place of Birth), y 461.88 (Fathers Name, Mothers Maiden Name, HusbandWifes Name). A band that occurs once is not a repetition. Test 3 - single-column stacks, which are the only recurring structures on this form: 2 found, and neither is a row group. Check Box1 to Check Box4 stack at x 81.454 width 18 (Part A, the four-way statutory fork) and Check Box5 to Check Box7 stack at x 44.8 width 18 (the three numbered affidavits). Each stack is ONE control per y - cols=1 - beside different printed statutory text, so they are mutually exclusive alternatives rather than repetitions of the same row. No group is split across dispositions in a way that could hide a half-written row, and that was checked rather than assumed: every member of both stacks is blank in both fixtures, with zero interior ink and zero ZapfDingbats glyphs. Because the form contains no repeating group, no row can carry a written cell beside a required cell left blank, and the obligation is satisfied by the absence rather than unmeasurable for it.
REPEATING_ROWS.priorMeasuredText: OCP-4 carries no repeating row structure. Its 23 widgets are 15 single text/signature fields and 7 independent selection controls, none of which forms a row of cells. There is no row on this packet that could carry a written cell beside a blank required cell.
REPEATING_ROWS.singleOccurrenceBandExamined: One thing the enumeration surfaces and this row states rather than leaves implicit. The single-occurrence identity band at y 501.96 has all four of its cells written on the canonical fixture (Mailing address, City 'Dorchester', State 'MA', Zip '02124') and, on the BOUNDARY fixture, two written beside two blank - Mailing address '1188 Upper Notch Crossing Road, Apartment 14B' and Zip '01103-2214' written, City and State blank. That is not an incomplete row and it is not what this obligation counts. The band is not a repeating group: it occurs once, its four cells carry four different printed captions, and it is a caption line of separate blanks rather than a row of a table. Both blanks are declared geometry refusals measured against the form's own box widths - 47 characters into a 100.08 pt box and 13 into a 40.08 pt box, refused whole at the 6 pt floor rather than shortened - and both are named to the participant in participant-instructions.md under 'Blanks the form itself is too small for', with the measurement and the instruction to write them in by hand. A packet that had truncated those values to fit would be the defect; refusing them whole and disclosing them is the designed behaviour.

observationsFromTheBytes.what: The petitioner's own name is the one held fact this petition does not print.
observationsFromTheBytes.measured: production-field-map.json's canonicalRefusals row for OCP-4/Print carries measurement.heldNameParts = {last: participant.last_name, first: participant.first_name, middle: participant.middle_name} and factId: null, and its prose says 'The platform holds your name and did not print it here'. The completeness contract's KNOWN_FACT_NOT_WRITTEN gate is keyed on dec.factAvailable, which verify-packet-completeness.mjs derives from the declared factId (line 380), so a row that names its held facts one level down in measurement and nulls factId cannot reach that gate. The refusal is nonetheless sound on the contract's stated terms, for the reason given under KNOWN_PREFILLS, and this lane did not score it as a defect.
observationsFromTheBytes.consequence: If the product later requires the name printed, the repair is a mechanism change and not a wording change: the shared finalizer would need a channel that places several facts at several measured x positions inside one widget rect - the three sub-caption x values (90, 203, 330) are already measured and re-checked against the binary on every build - instead of the newline join it has now. Nothing in this packet should be edited to satisfy the counter.
